Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then apply the required wake-visual inspection skill before touching the target policy. After that I’ll trace the assigned parent, sampled results, and inherited logs, produce one candidate, and update both required evidence files.

The README confirms this is a single-candidate, no-CFD worker, and the strongest sampled policies still fail by exiting left. I’m now using the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because the policy must be grounded in the available multi-wake keyframes before any code change.

The shared prewarm shows a fully developed four-street wake before release. Across the released sheets, the useful behavior is self-propelled upstream closing—not passive advection—but every sampled controller bends into the same upper-domain return before reaching the wake corridor. I’m cross-checking which policy terms changed and what the inherited optimizer logs actually attributed to those trajectories.

The decisive new comparison is now clear: the absolute fore/aft bearing-release policy is the best sampled finite result, but it and the assigned rearward-damping parent still end in essentially the same upper exit (`+1.80L` head-y). A normalized ahead gate is much worse and erases propulsion. I’m recording an isolated hypothesis that preserves the proven target-ahead law exactly and replaces only the aliased behind-target angle with a true full-circle body-frame heading error.

The candidate and durable lesson are now updated. The reusable takeaway is negative-but-specific: rearward bearing removal and rearward damping preserve the approach yet arrive too late, while normalized ahead gating activates early and destroys propulsion. The new candidate therefore changes only the post-beam target quadrant and leaves every established gait, steering, guard, and limiter value intact.

The first mandated check exposed a workspace-rendering defect before examining my changes: `README.md` lists the same copied guidance parent twice, while the checker requires exactly one marker. I’m inspecting the checker and immutable workspace metadata to resolve this without weakening the validation or touching out-of-scope solver files.

The guidance check now passes. The policy contract check is blocked by the runner environment rather than candidate code: `julia` is absent from `PATH` (the shell also emitted unrelated missing-SSH-directory setup warnings). I’m checking for the workspace’s Julia executable and will rerun the exact non-CFD assertion if one is available.

All three mandated non-CFD validations now pass: guidance provenance, Julia policy contract, and solver boundary. I’m doing a final scope/diff audit to confirm the candidate stayed non-empty, only one policy candidate exists, and the notes/guidance contain the intended evidence rather than any same-worker performance claim.

Produced exactly one 2D multi-wake policy candidate.

- [Candidate policy](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:29): preserves the proven target-ahead controller while using full-circle body-frame target heading after beam crossing.
- [Candidate reasoning](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) records the visual diagnosis, evidence, hypothesis, and falsification criteria.
- [Reusable lesson](guidance/control_experience.md:122) documents why rearward-only gating is too late and normalized ahead gating is destructive.

Guidance, Julia contract, parameter schema, and boundary checks pass. No CFD rollout was run. I also removed a duplicated assigned-parent entry from `README.md` that initially prevented the mandated guidance checker from running.
